data.title: AI becomes larger part of Stitch Fix strategy as Q4 revenue grows
data.description:
Stitch Fix returned to revenue growth in fiscal 2026, marking a milestone in the online styling retailer’s turnaround effort.

Customers spent more, while the company also pointed to growing adoption of its Vision AI tool.

For its fiscal 2026 ended Aug. 1, Stitch Fix generated $1.35 billion in net revenue, up 6.4% from $1.27 billion a year earlier. Its net loss narrowed to $12.6 million from $28.8 million in fiscal 2025. In Q4 alone, revenue rose 4.2% year over year to $324.4 million, marking Stitch Fix’s sixth consecutive quarter of positive revenue growth.

“Fiscal 2026 was a pivotal year for Stitch Fix,” CEO Matt Baer told analysts on the company’s Q4 earnings call. “We advanced our strategy and closed the year as a stronger, healthier business with a more resilient operating foundation and a reimagined client experience.”

The growth came despite a modest drop in active clients. Stitch Fix said it ended Q4 with roughly 2.28 million active clients, down 1.4% year over year. However, revenue per active client rose 7.8%, reaching a record $592.

At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a bigger part of Stitch Fix’s strategy. Baer highlighted growing adoption of the company’s Vision platform and discussed how Stitch Fix could one day participate in agentic shopping.

Stitch Fix is No. 78 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Stitch Fix is also No. 183 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Stitch Fix expands its AI-powered Vision tool

Baer said Stitch Fix’s 15 years of proprietary data and algorithms, paired with its human stylists, give the company a “foundation for incorporating AI across both the client experience and our operations.”

One of its most visible efforts is Stitch Fix Vision, the AI-powered style visualization tool the company launched a year ago. After customers upload photos through the app, Vision generates personalized images of them in curated outfits, with new looks added to their gallery each week.

Baer said Stitch Fix is integrating Vision more broadly across the shopping journey, letting customers see themselves in recommended looks from onboarding and Fix Preview through Freestyle and checkout.

A “fix” is Stitch Fix’s personalized shipment of clothing and accessories. Fix Preview lets customers review and change items before a Fix ships, while Freestyle lets them shop outside a scheduled shipment.

Customers who engage with Vision continue to show what Baer called a “significant lift” in 90-day Freestyle spending.

Since launch, Stitch Fix has shared more than 22 million Vision images with customers, Baer said.

More recently, Stitch Fix added See It On Me, an on-demand extension of Vision. Instead of waiting for new looks to appear in their gallery, customers browsing outfit suggestions in Freestyle can choose a look and see it rendered on their own likeness. Baer said Vision adoption has exceeded the company’s expectations. He added that See It On Me “helped considerably in terms of further expansion.”

Where Stitch Fix sees a role for AI shopping agents

Asked how Stitch Fix is positioning itself as AI reshapes shopping, Baer pointed to the company’s proprietary customer data as an advantage.

“At the end of the day, an AI experience, generative or agentic, the quality of that output is premised on the quality of the data that you put into it,” he said.

Baer also touched on the rise of agentic shopping, in which AI systems can take actions on a shopper’s behalf. Stitch Fix is “confident” it can participate in that shift, he said. He added that the company expects to serve either a human customer or an AI shopping agent. Baer did not provide details on how that would work.

Still, Baer argued that some purchases are better suited to automation than others.

“If I want to ensure my pantry is perpetually replenished with paper towels, that’s something I would happily outsource to my agentic shopper,” he said. Choosing clothes that fit, match someone’s style and budget and make them feel confident, he added, involves “a lot more nuance.”

That’s where Stitch Fix’s human stylists give it an advantage, he said.

“As more and more interactions for all consumers generally are taking place by AI, it is actually human connection (that) becomes the scarce resource,” Baer said.

At the same time, Stitch Fix is using AI behind the scenes to support employees. Generative AI tools now help stylists with item recommendations, he said. Meanwhile, AI assists with labor planning and real-time scheduling in its fulfillment centers. In customer service, AI agents handle more routine requests.

Baer said Stitch Fix has “more than doubled the share of chats resolved without requiring additional support.”

The company also recently hired Sree Sreedhararaj as chief product and technology officer. He previously served as chief technology officer at Ipsy. He oversaw an AI-powered personalization engine and agentic AI initiatives. Before that, he was chief technology officer at Sephora, where he led AI integration and personalization strategy, according to Stitch Fix’s announcement.

Stitch Fix customers spend more per client

Although Stitch Fix ended Q4 with fewer active clients than a year earlier, Baer said those trends continued to improve. The quarter marked the company’s ninth consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement in its active-client growth rate, he said.

At the same time, customers are spending more, on average. Baer attributed that partly to larger fixes and a wider assortment. These have supported eight consecutive quarters of growth in both items purchased per fix and average unit retail. Average order value (AOV) was the primary driver of Stitch Fix’s Q4 revenue growth, he added.

Stitch Fix is also expanding into categories where it historically has had a smaller presence, including activewear, athleisure, footwear and accessories. In Q4, activewear and athleisure sales grew 21% year over year, while footwear sales increased 14%, Baer said.

Since the start of fiscal 2026, Stitch Fix has also added more than 80 brands, including Birkenstock, Outdoor Voices and FARM Rio, he noted, as it expands its mix of market brands alongside its private labels.

Stitch Fix flags a tougher consumer environment in revenue forecast

Stitch Fix executives also pointed to higher customer acquisition costs as a headwind to bringing in and reengaging clients. Chief financial officer David Aufderhaar said those costs remained elevated into the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and are expected to weigh on client and revenue growth.

At the same time, existing customers are becoming more selective about discretionary purchases outside their recurring Fixes, Aufderhaar said. The company began seeing that pressure late in Q4 and expects those trends to factor into its full-year outlook.

For its fiscal Q1 2027, Stitch Fix expects revenue of $323 million to $328 million.

For the full fiscal 2027, Stitch Fix expects revenue of $1.31 billion to $1.36 billion.

Aufderhaar said its fiscal 2027 EBITDA outlook also reflects planned investments in advertising and technology, including AI, to support longer-term growth.

data.title: Ecommerce Trends: How Best Buy is using AI
data.description:
Best Buy is pushing artificial intelligence (AI) into areas of its operations in 2026, and its leadership team has described wider ambitions for how Best Buy will use AI to achieve near-term objectives.

In March, while speaking at the UBS Global Consumer and Retail Conference, Best Buy CEO Corie Barry called AI “a huge enabler of growth,” as well as for “good employee experiences.” At the time, she was addressing AI tools as internal resources for solving team members’ own problems. However, she also outlined how certain use cases will extend to customers as well.

Shoppers-facing AI deployments have since followed, notably with Best Buy opting to leverage OpenAI’s ChatGPT.

Best Buy ranks No. 8 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Best Buy is also No. 200 in Digital Commerce 360’s AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

How Best Buy is using AI internally

What is Best Buy’s Ask Blue shopping assistant?

In August, Best Buy detailed how it was rolling out its new customer-facing shopping assistant, Ask Blue. Jason Bonfig, senior executive vice president, chief customer and product and fulfillment officer at Best Buy, told analysts on the retailer’s Q2 earnings call that Ask Blue brought together multiple areas of expertise to enable outcomes for shoppers.

“Speaking of online experiences, I’m excited to announce the launch of Ask Blue, our new conversational AI shopping and support assistant,” he said during the call. “It brings together expertise from across Best Buy’s website in one easy-to-use experience.”

Altogether, Bonfig characterized Ask Blue as added value for online shoppers.

“It combines product knowledge, support, resources, customer reviews, availability and pricing to help customers make informed decisions,” he assessed. “Ask Blue will help customers figure out what tech is right for them.”

He cited examples such as comparing products, identifying important differences, checking compatibility and getting additional support. That may include connecting the shopper with a human support specialist.

Best Buy web sales by year

How Best Buy is working with OpenAI on agentic commerce

In addition, Best Buy has eyed new ways for online shoppers to discover its product listings through AI channels.

“We’re also continuing to partner with AI companies like OpenAI to make sure we are showing up in the places where our customers look for technology and advice,” Bonfig noted on the August earnings call. He is scheduled to replace Barry as Best Buy’s CEO on Nov. 1.

Bonfig described Best Buy’s recent “commerce integration with OpenAI,” which the company is promoting among its holiday plans for discovery and gift-buying.

“Customers can now discover products, receive recommendations and complete purchases for Best Buy directly within ChatGPT,” Bonfig told analysts. “We view this as an important step in expanding our digital ecosystem and positioning Best Buy at the forefront of emerging AI-enabled commerce experiences.”

data.title: Trane Technologies adds AI tools for repairs and part replacements
data.description:
Trane Technologies is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) offerings for building owners and facilities teams, including a new maintenance platform designed to centralize equipment records and maintenance workflows and help inform repair and replacement decisions.

The heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) and climate control equipment manufacturer announced that the offerings will span building analytics, maintenance management, connected controls and thermal management.

“As building operations become more connected and more complex, we’re evolving our AI and digital portfolio to help customers operate with greater clarity and control,” said Chris Tanaka, vice president of product management at Trane Technologies.

Trane Technologies’ Maintenance Manager

Maintenance Manager centralizes all the pieces that go into facility management. The company said it connects work orders, asset records, repair history and supporting documentation in one system.

Trane Technologies said it enables better coordination between service teams and more informed decisions about whether to repair aging equipment or begin planning for replacements.

“With Trane Cloud Analytics and Maintenance Manager, customers can connect building data, service workflows and asset history to support earlier action, better coordination and more informed planning,” Tanaka said. “Across the broader portfolio, these new solutions extend that same approach into controls and system management to help customers improve performance and reduce waste over time.”

The rest of Trane’s new product suite

And beyond Maintenance Manager, the Sept. 17 announcement covers several other tools.

Trane Cloud Analytics gives teams access to performance trends and efficiency gaps from connected building equipment. The company also designed a new Cloud Connected BACnet Thermostat to bring cloud-based building management to light commercial buildings that don’t have a full-building management system in place.

Tracer Zone Sensors are designed to simplify installation and setup for new construction and retrofit projects, and AI Control for Water Systems adjusts chiller plants to improve efficiency across existing infrastructure.

For data centers specifically, the announcement includes Chiller Plant Management and Data Hall Team Control. Both are designed to coordinate climate control over complex environments.

“As data center growth drives higher cooling loads, tighter performance requirements and faster response expectations, thermal management is becoming increasingly integral to uptime, efficiency and long-term infrastructure strategy,” said Oakley Roberts, president of data centers at Trane Technologies. “Intelligent, coordinated cooling systems are becoming essential to operating modern AI and mission-critical infrastructure at scale. These innovations help customers improve available capacity, strengthen resilience and maintain consistent thermal performance as computing demands continue to accelerate.”

How Trane got here

Trane has invested in AI technology for years. In 2024, Trane Technologies acquired BrainBox AI.

BrainBox AI is a Montreal-based company that had developed an AI platform to predict energy needs and automate HVAC operations. That acquisition built on a two-year collaboration between the companies. It also brought BrainBox’s predictive control capabilities directly into Trane’s product development pipeline.

In 2025, Trane opened a dedicated BrainBox AI lab and showroom focused on AI and energy management in buildings.

The investment in AI has occurred alongside growth for Trane. In its most recent fiscal quarter ended June 30, bookings were up 39% year over year. Meanwhile, net revenue grew 11% over the same period, to $6.35 billion.

data.title: Lowe's launches drone delivery in partnership with Wing, DoorDash
data.description:
Lowe’s said it has become the first home improvement retailer to offer drone delivery for online orders, working with Alphabet’s Wing and DoorDash on deliveries.

The newest fulfillment method delivers select home improvement products directly to Lowe’s DIY and Pro customers in as fast as 20 minutes, the retailer said. Its drone delivery pilot is now live at Lowe’s store in Matthews, North Carolina, and it adds to the retailer’s same-day fulfillment options. The other options include buy online, pick up in store (BOPIS), curbside pickup and same-day delivery.

Lowe’s is No. 9 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Lowe’s is also No. 90 in Digital Commerce 360’s new AI Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Products eligible for Lowe’s drone delivery

Lowe’s is offering drone delivery in partnership with Wing and DoorDash. Consumers can order Lowe’s products for delivery through the DoorDash app, which Wing drones will then deliver.

The retailer said its initial pilot is limited to “a curated list of eligible products.” The pilot program includes more than 100 SKUs. Those include:

  • All-purpose cleaner
  • Caulk
  • Hand tools
  • Household batteries
  • Paint products such as painter’s tape
  • Screwdrivers
  • Soap

Lowe’s said it’s testing its last-mile fulfillment by using its physical stores as hubs for staging drone dispatch areas. That process integrates DoorDash’s third-party marketplace demand into specialized drone delivery, the retailer said.

Lowe’s said the drone delivery pilot builds on its broader efforts to use technology to remove friction from home improvement. It noted Mylow, Lowe’s AI assistant for customers, and Mylow Companion, its AI-powered assistant for store associates, as recent innovations. Together, the two assistants have helped answer more than 25 million questions since launching in 2025, according to Lowe’s.

“Home improvement is an inherently friction-filled experience,” said Seemantini Godbole, chief information and AI officer at Lowe’s. “Any technology we implement is designed to eliminate that friction so our customers can complete their projects quickly. By piloting drone delivery, we’re addressing a real project pain point with an innovative solution that is integrated into the retail journey, giving our hometown customers next-generation fulfillment right when they need it.”

data.title: JD Sports deploys Algolia for agentic commerce strategy
data.description:
JD Sports has deployed Algolia as the retailer’s governing intelligence layer on which to build its agentic commerce strategy.

Announced Sept. 22, the companies seek to enable product discovery and shopping through agentic artificial intelligence (AI) platforms. JD Sports initially implemented Algolia into its tech stack in 2024.

Since then, JD Sports said:

  • Revenue from search has increased 22%.
  • Search click-through rates have increased 7.65%.
  • Product listing page (PLP) click-through rates have increased 73%.
  • PLP revenue has increased 16%.

JD Sports is No. 28 in the Europe Database. The market research tool tracks the region’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

The retailer said it operates more than 4,800 stores globally. It also has more than 9 million active loyalty program members.

Algolia said it primes JD Sports’ catalog so AI agents can find the answers they need for “conversational, intent-heavy queries.” Still, it uses the same catalog and ranking logic that powers JD Sports’ website.

JD Sports said as its ecommerce operations and product catalogs expanded, merchandising teams were spending “significant time manually tuning results, boosting products and maintaining static rules.” That model could not keep up with shifting trends, seasonality and shopper behavior, according to the companies.

JD Sports, working with Algolia Professional Services, moved its website to a MACH ecommerce architecture. MACH is an acronym referring to four technology principles:

  1. Microservices. This refers to individual, small features that run as independent services rather than part of one large codebase.
  2. API-first. Features communicate through application programming interfaces (APIs). That enables merchants to plug in third-party tools.
  3. Cloud-native. The site fully runs on the cloud.
  4. Headless. The front end is separate from the back end.

“Replacing a highly manual search and merchandising process with an AI-native foundation changed how we operate…,” said Kristin Matter, vice president of digital operations at JD Sports. “We respond faster to changing shopper behavior and emerging trends, our merchandisers spend their time on strategy instead of tuning, and the revenue gains follow.”

How JD Sports is optimizing for agentic commerce

JD Sports now uses dynamic re-ranking (DRR). That means it uses real-time click and conversion signals to identify trending products and automatically adjust their placement, the companies explained. It does so within merchandising rules that JD Sports’ team defines. The retailer can see and reverse each adjustment.

The retailer saw a 2.2% increase in click-through rate from DRR. Additionally, DRR led to a 4% increase in JD Sports’ add-to-cart rate as well as 4% growth in its conversion rate.

JD Sports and Algolia said they’ve begun using AI “to proactively surface” emerging search trends, inventory shifts and merchandising opportunities. They also have been using it “to tailor discovery to individual shopper intent.”

The same process that displays search results now works for AI agents, the companies explained. That gives JD Sports a way to “control relevance” across shopping channels.

“JD Sports understood before most that discovery is a growth engine, not a website feature, and a 22% lift in search revenue is a P&L result, not an IT metric,” said Stephen Lynch, CEO at Algolia.

Lynch said in a category where demand shifts weekly, “winning takes intelligence merchandisers can inspect and control, not a black box they’re asked to trust.”

He added that he sees the next wave of retail growth going to the companies whose catalogs agents can shop. To enable that, retailers have to make their catalogs structured, current and accurate, he said.
